parsed.explanation: Combined operative regime: national Penal Code ss.377A/377B (up to 20 years plus whipping, applied to tourists) overlays state Sharia enactments barring Muslim men from 'dressing as women' and enforced by religious departments with no legal definition. Documented state-directed targeting is the decisive feature: a 2020 ministerial licence to hunt trans persons, a 2021 mobilisation of 122 officers against a trans woman, and a 2025 raid arresting 208 men with leaked personal details, including 31 foreign nationals held. Custody carries documented male-ward sexual violence. Gender-marker changes are routinely refused, so documents cannot be made to match. Court remedies have been partial and federalism-based only. The 2019 killing is dated, with no trans-specific rate. Rating reflects known organised targeting and universal document exposure with no working remedy for visitors.

entry_documents.exposure: Registration Department routinely rejects gender-marker changes, so visitors' documents may not match presentation. No explicit visa rule for trans visitors; 2001 deportation remark on gay cabinet members is unsourced for current operation.
entry_documents.interaction: Document mismatch at checkpoints can trigger questioning and the enforcement pathway into police or religious custody.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: 2025 raid: 208 arrested under s.377B, over 130 held at one point, 31 foreign nationals. Prison terms of 4 months to 3 years with male-ward sexual violence. 2011 strip-search and sexual assault by religious officials.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Magistrate rejected remand extension; embassies intervened; legal-aid organisation mobilised bail. These helped detainees but did not prevent detention.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Tourists are liable under federal penal code while religious enforcement applies to Muslims; a foreign Muslim visitor faces both layers.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Federal penal liability reaches all persons. State religious codes operate in all 13 units. Federal court struck some state provisions on federalism grounds, but federal Penal Code liability is untouched; High Court refused to strike cross-dressing ban.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Partial: state provisions struck in 2021 and 2024 on constitutional grounds.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Removing state provisions does not reduce the federal s.377 exposure, so the harshest operative rule still governs.

care_services.exposure: Discriminatory denial of health care documented. 1982 fatwa bars Muslims from sex-reassignment surgery (not gazetted, operation unresolved). Blood donation ban for homosexual and bisexual people.
care_services.interaction: Care-seeking can bring the traveller into the same registries and enforcement channels.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: State threat-framing: government ministers and religious leaders promote conversion therapy; 2020 licence for religious enforcement against trans persons; government-funded rehabilitation retreats (1,733 attendees by 2021); censorship of LGBT content; 1994 media ban.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Hate-speech code covers orientation but is not an anti-discrimination or hate-crime remedy.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Official framing raises the probability that outing leads to state action, including by media tip-offs.

minors_guardians.exposure: Religious counselling or rehabilitation orders up to one year (Terengganu 2022, Kelantan and Pahang up to six months) apply to offenders; a minor travelling with a guardian could be exposed through document or presentation checks. Not documented for minors specifically.
minors_guardians.protection: Adoption is orientation-neutral (not a visitor factor).
minors_guardians.interaction: A guardian's arrest could separate a minor from a parent; no youth-specific finding in the dossier.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: 2019 killing of a trans woman, one of three in under two months, with police mistreatment and impunity. Raids on queer venues (2018, 2022, 2023). No trans-specific violence rate against the general homicide rate.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Enforcement against consenting adults in private described as uncommon; tourists rarely targeted (practical guide).
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Police response to victims is documented as impunity, so reporting is not a reliable remedy.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No anti-discrimination or hate-crime law. Remedies are inconsistent: 2016 identity judgment overturned in 2017; Registration Department rejects changes. Post-2025 minister floated revisiting provisions, but no reform is in force.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Partial court wins on federalism grounds only; reform prospects blocked by Islamist opposition.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Recourse exists in form but does not change outcomes for the outed traveller.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar: arrests for presentation-related impersonation, prisoner and guard assaults on trans detainees, and no effective appeal. This dossier is comparable in custody and targeting but lacks the documented capital provision for this case, so it sits slightly higher.

Lower: birth-sex housing, presentation-based arrests and unmonitored custody match the dossier's custody exposure. This dossier adds explicit state licence for religious hunts and mass raids with foreign nationals held, which pushes it below 0.25.

Lower: 0.35-B has police stops and interviews with detention rarely becoming imprisonment. This dossier documents multi-year imprisonment, male-ward sexual violence and mass raids, which are materially more severe.

parsed.synthesis: Federal penal liability (up to 20 years plus whipping) applies to visitors regardless of state remedies, and state religious enforcement is documented as targeting trans people. Discovery is facilitated by refused gender-marker changes and by media tip-offs during raids. Consequences documented in custody include male-ward sexual violence, with foreign detainees held in large numbers. Oversight and court relief have been partial and federalism-based, and they have not changed enforcement. The 2019 killing is dated and no trans-specific violence rate is available, so violence weighs as documented but not quantified. The rating sits in the High Risk band.
